tlfstack

tlfstack is a convention stack for clinical tables, listings and figures (TLFs) in R: the reporting conventions a SAS shop keeps in ODS templates and a macro library, written as R code and metadata.

It rests on two design principles:

  1. One code path, two modes. Builders are pure functions: data in, a table object or ggplot out. They never read data, write files or touch metadata. A scheduled batch program and an interactive Shiny preview make the same call and get the same RTF content. The two modes differ only at the data entry point and the output exit point.
  2. Metadata shared across languages. Titles, footnotes and output file names come from one table of contents (TOC). This can be the same database table your SAS programs read, a snapshot of it, or a version-controlled JSON/YAML file. Because both sides read one source string, the title blocks match by construction.

What is in the stack

Layer Functions
Configuration tlf_config(), tlf_page(), tlf_fonts(), tlf_render_opts(), tlf_get_config() (argument > options() > TLFSTACK_CONFIG file > defaults)
Builders tbl_demographics(), tbl_ae(), tbl_ae_severity(), tbl_disposition(), tbl_eff(), tbl_shift(), tbl_tte(), tbl_listing(); fig_meanci(), fig_boxplot(), fig_spaghetti(), fig_lsmeans(), fig_km(), fig_forest(), fig_waterfall(), fig_edish(), fig_shift()
Dispatcher tlf_build_table(), tlf_build_figure(), tlf_register_table(), tlf_register_figure()
Titles and TOC tlf_titles(), tlf_resolve_titles() (live, then snapshot, then fallback), toc_source_db(), toc_source_file(), toc_source_dir(), toc_read(), toc_write()
Convention engine theme_tlf_submission(), tlf_rtf_table(), tlf_rtf_listing(), tlf_rtf_figure()
Crash isolation tlf_run_isolated(): figure rendering in a callr child process with bounded retries and an attempt log

Example 

library(tlfstack)

# Organization conventions, set once per session (for example in a site profile).
options(tlfstack.config = tlf_config(header_left = "Example Organization"))

# Titles from a TOC: a live DBI source first, then a snapshot file.
titles <- tlf_resolve_titles(
  "t_demo",
  sources = list(toc_source_dir("metadata")),   # or toc_source_db(connector, "toc")
  scope = list(study = "STUDY01")
)

# The same call a Shiny app makes.
res <- tlf_build_table("demographics", list(adsl = ex_adsl))
tlf_rtf_table(res, file.path(tempdir(), titles$output_file_name), titles = titles)

Title metadata as a file

toc_write() dumps any TOC, including a live database table, to JSON or YAML for offline work, code review and other languages:

tlfstack_toc: 1
generated_at: 2026-10-22T09:00:00+0000
source: database
outputs:
  - program: t_demo
    scope: {study: STUDY01}
    type: Table
    number: "14.1.1"
    title: [Summary of Demographic and Baseline Characteristics]
    subtitle: [Safety Population]
    footnotes: [Percentages are based on the number of subjects in each column.]
    output_file_name: t-14-01-01-demog.rtf

The format has a published JSON Schema: system.file("schema", "tlfstack-toc-v1.schema.json", package = "tlfstack").

Where tlfstack sits

tlfstack does not replace the table-construction or interactive-review packages. Its scope is what sits around them:

  • rtables, gtsummary, Tplyr build table bodies. tlfstack renders pre-formatted data frames, so a body from any of them can go through its renderers.
  • tfrmt expresses a table’s layout as metadata for review before database lock. tlfstack adds page and figure conventions and TOC-driven titles for locked output. The two are complementary.
  • teal is interactive exploration. tlfstack’s interactive mode is a preview of the production output.
  • chevron generates standard TLF programs. tlfstack is a shared runtime layer that both batch and interactive code call.
  • r2rtf is the RTF engine tlfstack builds on.

No single feature here is new. The contribution is the combination: one code path for batch and interactive work, conventions as code, one metadata source shared with SAS, and crash-tolerant figure rendering.

Installation

tlfstack is not yet on CRAN.
